subject: Harmonized ramp safeguards & auto-renew playbook for ACME renewal
messages:
From: Tom Harper <tom.harper@acme.ai>

Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.ai>
Date: 2025-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — need to lock term + burst guard

Camila,

Our renewal for the platform is coming up at the end of November and we want to avoid the surprises we saw last year when burst usage pushed us into a higher tier mid-quarter. Two asks from my side: 1) can we structure a multi-year renewal with a controlled ramp that allows some burst without auto-upgrading our committed tier, and 2) can we add a safeguard so auto-renew doesn't kick in with an unintended volume spike?

High level: current annual commitment 12M tokens/month steady-state, occasional 3x burst for new features. We expect steady growth (~10% yoy) and an upcoming pilot in Q1 that could temporarily double usage for 6-8 weeks.

Can we schedule a 30 min sync this week to walk the options (ramp schedule, guard rails, and any discount/credit constructs)? Sara will join from procurement.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harper
Head of Platform Operations
Acme AI

Attachment: usage-export-202509.csv (referenced)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harper <tom.harper@acme.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — need to lock term + burst guard

Tom — thanks for the clear context. Sara — welcome.

Short answer: yes, we can do a multi-year with an explicit ramp and a burst-safeguard that prevents automatic tier escalation during short-term spikes. Suggested high-level construct I shared below:

- Term: 24 months co-term with fiscal year-end option (your choice).
- Ramp schedule: year 1 = 100% baseline (12M tokens/mo), year 2 = baseline + 20% (so 14.4M tokens/mo).
- Burst buffer: each month you get a 50% temporary buffer above committed usage for up to 6 weeks per rolling 12 months without changing commitment.
- Auto-renew guard: auto-renew will still occur unless explicitly opted out, but we add a "Usage Trigger Review" window — any month with sustained >2x baseline for 60 days will open a manual review before changing tier or billing.
- Credits: for any sustained sustained overshoot beyond guard for a month we can apply a one-time credit to smooth the first occurrence (proofed by usage logs).

I've attached a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MA) + a simple calc sheet that models burst scenarios and invoice impact (attached: ACME_MA_draft_v1.pdf, usage-bands-calc.xlsx).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30 min sync to align on preference for co-term vs. fixed 24mo starting contract date.
2) Confirm acceptable burst buffer (50% default; can be tuned).
3) Marissa (cc'd) will confirm discount band and final contract language we recommend for the guard.

If that sounds good, I'm free Thurs 1–3pm or Friday morning PST.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Renewal coming up — need to lock term + burst guard

Looping in pricing guidance and a couple of internal notes.

Camila — good structure. A few things from pricing/SE side:
- Discount: for a 24mo with the ramp described, recommend a 12–15% blended discount across the term with a mid-term true-up window.
- Guard language: change "manual review" wording to "Usage Review & Escalation Process" and specify an operational SLA: Redwood will notify within 5 business days of a trigger and propose options (apply temporary credit, propose short-term top-up, or engage usage engineering).
- Burst buffer: 50% default OK, but add a carve-out that excludes prototype spikes tied to new feature launches if they can be scoped (we'll require a calendar notice for expected pilot windows).

Inline to Camila's email:
> - Auto-renew guard: auto-renew will still occur unless explicitly opted out, but we add a "Usage Trigger Review" window...

Recommend we offer two flavors to Acme:
A) Conservative: 24mo, 10% discount, 50% monthly buffer, 1x smoothing credit (covers first sustained overage event), opt-out auto-renew by written notice 30 days prior.
B) Growth-friendly: 36mo, 15% discount, 75% buffer for newly launched pilots (with calendar notice), automatic true-up at 6 months, auto-renew only with an agreed renewal playbook.

Marissa — help us land which flavor is approvable. If Acme wants the Growth-friendly path we should also lock a minimum ARR floor to protect RL economics.

Karthik
VP, Customer Growth | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

1) Buffer: 60% buffer for pilot windows (instead of 75%) and we will provide calendar notices for any planned pilot windows;
2) Minimum ARR floor: we'll accept a 2% ARR floor applied only if year-two growth exceeds modeled ramp (protects you).
